data.description:
OnTrac is hiring a Senior Enterprise Architect!

Are you eager to join a dynamic and expanding company where you can both learn and make a meaningful impact? If you possess a strong sense of empathy, enjoy assisting others, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and excel at problem-solving, we encourage you to apply today to connect with a recruiter!

Founded in 1986, OnTrac has evolved into the leading provider of same-day and next-day delivery services in the U.S. for premier e-commerce and product-supply businesses, including five of the largest retailers in the U.S.

Location:

REMOTE: This position may be performed remotely in states where the company is authorized to employ individuals.

Compensation:

The expected starting base pay range for this position is $180,000 - $225,000, with full potential base salary range over a successful candidate’s tenure in the position of $180,000 - $270,000. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, internal equity, and other job-related factors. This position may also be eligible for bonus, commission, or other incentive compensation in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan of up to a 25% Bonus Target.

Employment Logistics:

Reporting to the CTO, this position is a hands-on, highly technical architect responsible for designing and building the AI-native platform, data, and integration architecture that powers OnTrac’s last mile delivery network. Working across platform, core, and domain engineering teams, this position defines the target-state architecture on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) for generative AI, agentic workflows, and real-time data, proves designs through proofs of concept and reference implementations, and partners with engineers to take them into production. The role brings deep expertise in LLM frameworks, Model Context Protocol (MCP), multi-agent systems, data engineering, API management, architecture patterns, and DevOps and LLMOps, and keeps the organization at the forefront of rapidly evolving AI technology.

Unpacking the Benefits:

Employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package which may include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life and short- and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match
  • Flex vacation in states other than CA, CO, IL, MA, MT, and NE, with accruals up to 96 hours for first year of employment with tenure-based increases up to 160 hours
  • Two (2) floating holidays per year
  • Paid sick leave*
  • Six (6) paid company holidays
  • Two (2) weeks paid pregnancy disability leave, four (4) weeks paid parental bonding leave
  • Additional wellness and employee assistance programs

Benefits eligibility and offerings are subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans and company policies.

The Must-Haves:

This position requires a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent and 10 years of relevant experience in software engineering, data engineering, or solution architecture, including at least 7 years in an architecture role and 2 years of hands-on generative AI or LLM solution delivery. MUST HAVE 3 years of hands-on experience designing, building, and running production solutions on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). MUST HAVE 3 years of experience in the last mile delivery, parcel, or logistics industry, supporting technology for delivery operations such as route planning, sortation, scanning, tracking, or driver and dispatch systems. MUST HAVE experience designing and implementing enterprise API management and integration platforms, such as Apigee, MuleSoft, Kong, or Azure API Management.

Success in this role requires:

  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of agentic AI, including agent frameworks (such as Google ADK, LangGraph, or CrewAI), multi-agent orchestration, tool and function calling, agent memory, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and agent-to-agent (A2A) protocols.
  • Expert knowledge of GCP architecture and its AI and data services, such as Vertex AI, Gemini, Vertex AI Vector Search, BigQuery, Dataflow, Pub/Sub, GKE, Cloud Run, and Apigee.
  • Expert knowledge of data engineering for AI, including data modeling, batch and stream processing, ETL/ELT, change data capture (CDC), lakehouse design, feature and vector stores, data quality, and data governance.
  • Strong knowledge of API management and integration, including API design standards, gateways, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, event streaming with Kafka and Pub/Sub, and exposing APIs as tools for AI agents.
  • Strong DevOps, MLOps, and LLMOps skills, including Terraform, CI/CD tooling (such as GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or Cloud Build), Kubernetes, model and prompt versioning, automated evaluation, and LLM observability tools.
  • Understanding of last mile delivery and parcel logistics, including the parcel lifecycle, scan events, network planning, routing, geospatial data, and driver and carrier operations, and where AI creates value in each.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, balance hands-on engineering with architectural leadership, and prioritize multiple initiatives.

Google Cloud Professional certifications, such as Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Machine Learning Engineer, or Professional Data Engineer and experience establishing an AI center of excellence, agent platform, or reference architectures and standards in a product-led technology organization are strongly preferred.

Your Mission in Motion:

A summary of key responsibilities for the role is outlined below. Additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business objectives.

  • Define and own the target-state architecture for OnTrac’s AI-native logistics platform on GCP, spanning shared platform services, reusable core services, domain applications, and the AI and agent layer that runs across them.
  • Design and build agentic and multi-agent systems, including agent orchestration, planning and tool use, memory and state management, human-in-the-loop controls, and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication.
  • Architect the MCP server ecosystem that exposes core logistics services (orders, shipments, tracking, locations, routing) and enterprise data as governed, reusable tools for internal and external AI agents.
  • Design AI-ready data platforms, including batch and real-time streaming pipelines, lakehouse and warehouse architectures, feature stores, and vector stores, using services such as BigQuery, Dataflow, Pub/Sub, Spanner, AlloyDB, and Vertex AI Vector Search.
  • Define a canonical, unified data model and event taxonomy for orders, shipments, scan events, locations, containers, and drivers, published as versioned contracts and as semantic context for LLMs and agents, with data quality, lineage, and governance built in.
  • Define the API and integration architecture, including API-first design, REST, gRPC, and asynchronous APIs, OpenAPI and AsyncAPI contracts, API management through Apigee, and event-driven integration over Pub/Sub and Kafka, serving applications and AI agents alike.
  • Apply and document architecture patterns for distributed and AI systems, including microservices, domain-driven design, event sourcing, CQRS, and saga, alongside agentic patterns such as ReAct, planner-executor, supervisor and router agents, and advanced RAG, and publish reference architectures for engineering teams.
  • Build proofs of concept, prototypes, and reference implementations hands-on to validate new models, agent frameworks, and AI tools, de-risk designs, and move quickly from experiment to production; write production-quality code alongside engineering teams.

data.title: Platform Engineer - Compute Capacity
data.description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a platform engineer to join our Compute Capacity team. This team owns the capacity plan that keeps compute supply ahead of demand across every region we operate in — the forecasting, buffer policy, and provisioning systems that make sure a project never runs into a wall it didn't know was there.

You'll work on the systems that turn a capacity plan into provisioned reality: reservation acquisition, fleet reconciliation, and the automation that keeps what we've committed to in sync with what we're actually running. You'll help build the metrics and alerting that let capacity problems surface months out, on vendor lead time, rather than at the moment someone needs the room.

You'll design, build, and operate systems that are both robust and highly automated — helping us hold the right buffer at the right cost, catch drift before it becomes a shortage, and give every team a single, trustworthy view of how much room we have across the millions of databases we manage.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Help build and maintain the capacity plan that keeps Supabase's compute supply ahead of demand across regions and instance families

  • Support buffer policy by modeling headroom targets and their cost tradeoffs for review and sign-off

  • Build and maintain automation that turns the capacity plan into provisioned reality — reservation acquisition and top-up, fleet reconciliation, drift detection between committed and running capacity

  • Extend our infrastructure as code for capacity-relevant provisioning

  • Instrument capacity: build and maintain metrics for saturation, reservation coverage, idle buffer, forecast error, and provisioning latency

  • Build and tune capacity alerting so headroom, quota, and reservation issues surface months out rather than at the moment of impact

  • Support the demand gate — helping intake large customer commitments, launches, migrations, and new regions so they reach the plan before they reach the fleet

  • Contribute to mitigation projects: right-sizing, instance-family migrations, autoscaling improvements, workload consolidation

  • Help drive down compute cost per database through right-sizing, placement, and commitment coverage work

  • Participate in capacity incident response and post-incident follow-through

You Might Be A Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years across infrastructure engineering, SRE, platform, or capacity engineering, ideally at SaaS or cloud infrastructure scale

  • Have production software engineering experience — you've owned and operated a service, not just a notebook. Comfortable in modern languages like TypeScript, Python, and Go

  • Are comfortable working against forecasts and assumptions that are incomplete, and can revise your work as those assumptions change

  • Have experience with Infrastructure as Code (Pulumi or Terraform)

  • Have built or maintained observability for systems you own — metrics that answer real questions and alerting people trust (Prometheus/Grafana, CloudWatch, or similar);

  • Have solid working knowledge of AWS EC2: instance families and generations, purchase options, capacity reservations, and quota mechanics

  • Have some financial fluency — you understand reservation economics and the basic tradeoffs between coverage, utilization, and cost

  • Communicate clearly across audiences, from engineers to finance stakeholders

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Moodle with us!

At Moodle, we’re on a mission to empower educators and learners worldwide with open, flexible, and innovative digital learning solutions. As the world’s most customizable and trusted open-source LMS, we partner with schools, universities, and organizations to create better learning experiences for millions. If you’re ready to make a real impact, and be part of a global movement shaping the future of learning, join us. Let's transform education together!

About the Role

Join our team as the Senior Manager, DevOps and become a key leader in delivering cutting-edge technology for our external customers, vendors, and clients. You will manage a fully remote high-performing team dedicated to maintaining and optimizing our critical infrastructure, ensuring peak performance and security. This includes overseeing stability and performance tuning, customer upgrades and migrations, and implementing robust security measures. You will be instrumental in managing the customer support requests and guaranteeing seamless, 24-hour monitoring and support. This is an exciting opportunity to expand the business and make a significant impact on our technology delivery.

Senior Manager, DevOps - Drive Innovation and Infrastructure Excellence (US)

Managing the delivery of technology for external customers, vendors, and other clients to improve and expand the business, the Senior Manager, DevOps is responsible for managing the team maintaining our infrastructure to perform optimally including: maintaining stability of systems, proactive monitoring, servicing customer support requests, removal of technical debt, and being part of a team that pushes our infrastructure forward.

This role will support important security certification projects and work within federal client boundaries. Successful applicants must be US citizens with willingness and ability to receive necessary security clearances.

What You’ll Do

Most days in this role usually involve a mix of:

  • Support DevOps team in managing client hosting infrastructure
  • Lead the team in best practices for deployment, availability, performance and automation
  • Manage and participate in the on-call rotation as needed
  • Provide technical expertise, recommendations and evaluations to the management team
  • Assist with coordinating tasks that need to be completed as part of certification processes and procedures as required (SOC2, FedRamp, ISO, etc.)
  • Assist in the development and implementation of department wide operational policies including security, process, and support policies
  • Assist Sales with scoping and pricing non-standard implementations and infrastructure requests
  • Manage the DevOps team to ensure the availability and reliability of the Moodle Services hosting platforms
  • Coach and mentor DevOps team members
  • Manage and prioritize team workloads, including managing incoming support and infrastructure requests
  • Represent the DevOps team in customer facing meetings where required
  • Review priorities and with the Global Head of Infrastructure to align work with strategic priorities
  • Represent the DevOps team to the wide company
  • Be responsible for the career development and performance of direct reports

We’d love to meet you

Especially if you can tell us about your:

  • Extensive experience as a technical lead or manager leading complex, distributed, and remote teams, particularly in large scale environments
  • Strong customer facing skills
  • Working experience using modern team management methodologies. Agile, SCRUM, are preferred
  • Knowledge of best practices related to high availability, fault tolerance, performance and disaster recovery
  • 5 years of Linux/Unix system administration experience and AWS hosted infrastructure
  • Knowledge of Python, PHP, shell scripting or other scripting languages an advantage
  • Extensive experience troubleshooting network, system and application issues
  • Amazing problem solving, analysis and communication skills
  • Being available for on-call support and occasional out of hours work
  • US citizenship with willingness and ability to obtain appropriate security clearances for US government projects.

Experience in the following areas is a plus:

  • Configuring and supporting monitoring tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, NewRelic.
  • Experience with configuration management and IaC
  • Experience working in a FedRAMP environment.

What's in it for you?

Moodle has a globally diverse team with over 280 team members in more than 25 countries around the world. We’ve built a passionate team of hard-working, driven and diverse people from all over the world, united by a shared belief in the ability of our platform to make a positive difference to our world. We respect our colleagues and value an open and innovative workplace, filled with integrity and of course a strong focus on education (yes, these are our company values!)

In addition to this you can expect:

  • Working with a remote first company, taking on a genuinely flexible, distributed role.

  • Health insurance plans to fit your life, with up to 100% employer contribution, as well as vision, dental, and group life and AD&D. Plus a wide variety of voluntary insurances.
  • Working with a global team on a worldwide platform to make a real difference.

Learn more about Moodle

Moodle is the world’s most trusted online learning solution, with a growing ecosystem of products and services, including Moodle Workplace, Moodle App, MoodleCloud, and more. The engine of our ecosystem is Moodle LMS, the secure and customizable open source learning management platform used by well over 300 million learners worldwide.

Find out more about us on our website.

Location:Remote

Job Type:Full-time

About Us!

At Ready Computing, we specialize in data-centric IT solutions that help organizations across healthcare, supply chain, finance, and manufacturing optimize their technology and data strategies. With offices in the U.S. and the UK, we provide expert consulting, development, and managed services to clients worldwide. We're committed to hiring top talent to drive innovation, particularly in the healthcare IT space.

The Software Architect designs Wellbase, Ready Computing’s managed services suite for healthcare and social-care organizations, and remains hands-on through implementation. Wellbase provides hosting, monitoring, analytics, and security to keep mission-critical systems available, secure, and improving. This player-coach role involves designing and owning end-to-end solutions while leading a small delivery team.

The work includes Wellbase’s agentic AI companion (Lucas), governed and auditable Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, policy and governance services, and product demonstration and staging environments. The role calls for curiosity about emerging technologies, confidence presenting architecture and tradeoffs to executives, and a strong sense of ownership.

What you'll do

Essential duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Define technical requirements and target architecture for new platform capabilities, and stay accountable through design, implementation, and release.
  • Design and lead delivery of agentic AI solutions, including tool-using agents, evaluation approaches, and safe integration with healthcare workflows.
  • Architect and extend MCP-based services that connect agents and applications to enterprise systems, data, and licensed capabilities.
  • Own architecture for policy and governance services that control access, content decisions, and regulated use of data and AI.
  • Shape the architecture of demo and staging environments so new capabilities can be shown reliably to customers and executives.
  • Lead a small team as a player-coach: set technical direction, review design and code, and implement the hardest pieces yourself.
  • Present architecture, options, and recommendations to executive stakeholders; take ownership of decisions and outcomes.
  • Apply CI/CD, cloud, and Kubernetes deployment practices to keep the platform releasable and operable.
  • Mentor developers and raise the quality bar for design, security, and delivery.
  • Produce and maintain technical documentation that others can build from.
  • Design and optimize data stores (relational and, where needed, vector or other specialized stores) to support agents, applications, and governance.
  • Implement authorization, policy, and security controls appropriate to healthcare and other regulated data.
  • Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

What you bring

Technical Skills

  • Expertise in software architecture and design patterns for cloud-native and service-based enterprise systems.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and/or Java, with the ability to work across a polyglot stack.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (Google Cloud preferred), containers, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • Experience designing REST APIs and distributed services; familiarity with workflow or orchestration systems is a plus.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and development tools such as Git, Jenkins, and JIRA.
  • Database design and optimization, primarily relational (PostgreSQL); exposure to vector or search stores is a plus.
  • Familiarity with enterprise frameworks such as Spring or FastAPI.
  • Working knowledge of policy-as-code, authorization frameworks, or similar governance controls is a plus.
  • Some hands-on experience with agentic AI development (LLM-based agents, tool use or MCP, evaluation design, or similar).
  • Familiarity with observability and monitoring technologies such as Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry (OTel).
  • Demonstrated curiosity and a track record of evaluating and adopting new technologies where they create real leverage.

Qualaifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Software Development, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 8 years of software development experience with a focus on enterprise-level architectures, including hands-on design and implementation. Some experience building or leading agentic AI solutions is required.
  • Comfort working with healthcare or other regulated data environments.
  • Deep healthcare-interoperability experience is helpful but not required.

Core Competencies

  • Technical Architectural Leadership: Architects scalable, future-ready solutions and leads a small team through implementation, remaining hands-on on the hardest work.
  • Solution Ownership: Takes end-to-end accountability for designs and outcomes, from first concept through delivery and operation.
  • Curiosity and Innovation: Actively explores new technologies and approaches, especially in agentic AI and platform engineering, and applies them with sound judgment.
  • Executive Communication: Presents architecture, options, and recommendations clearly to executive audiences, and translates complex technical concepts for diverse stakeholders.
  • Analytical Problem-Solving: Diagnoses and resolves intricate technical challenges in order to keep programs moving.
  • Attention to Detail & Security: Maintains rigorous standards in design and development to ensure the reliability, scalability, and security of enterprise solutions.

Physical & Mental Qualifications:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

  • All positions require the ability to work on a computer for extended periods of time, including typing, using a mouse, and viewing a monitor throughout an eight (8) hour workday. Employees must be able to sit and/or stand for prolonged periods, as needed to perform their duties.
  • Positions may involve infrequent lifting of items such as a laptop or related equipment. Walking requirements are limited to normal travel or commute needs as outlined in this section.
  • All roles require the ability to communicate effectively, including speaking on the phone and collaborating with team members, clients, vendors, and other business partners. Employees must be able to focus on multiple tasks and project requirements throughout the workday. Most positions may require occasional travel.

Home Office Requirements

  • A minimum internet speed of 25 Mbps for downloads and 1.5 Mbps for uploads is required.
  • A private Wi-Fi network with a strong, unique password is necessary to access company data or systems.
  • The company provides a monthly internet stipend. New hires must complete a speed test during onboarding and update any default router passwords to ensure secure network access.

Why Join Us?

Innovative & Impactful Work – Your contributions will shape healthcare technology and improve patient outcomes.

Global Reach & Growth Opportunities – Work with leading experts in healthcare IT and enterprise solutions.

Collaborative & Dynamic Culture – Join a supportive team environment that values knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and career development.

Competitive salary and benefits package, including:

  • Four health plan options to fit your needs.
  • 401(k) matching to help secure your financial future.
  • Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO) for work-life balance.
  • Wellness programs to support your mental and physical well-being.
  • Financial planning services to help you manage your future.

Ready to Apply?

If you’re excited about healthcare IT, system integration, and building next-gen interoperability solutions, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now or contact for more information.

Ready Computing is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and Affirmative Action (AA) employer. We are committed to EEO for all protected classes, individuals with disabilities, and protected veterans. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by any law.

About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is embarking on a journey to build the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Infrastructure team is central to this mission, setting the core strategy and implementing the vision. We design and operate mission-critical facilities that support cutting-edge AI workloads at scale.

About the Role

We are seeking a Critical Facilities Lead to support the commissioning, deployment, and long-term operation of our next-generation AI data centers. This role bridges the interface between data center construction and hardware landing, ensuring seamless integration of mission-critical infrastructure with hardware deployment timelines. You will define and execute commissioning plans, support infrastructure bring-up, and take ownership of operations and maintenance for cutting-edge, large-scale, AI data centers.

You will collaborate closely with design, construction, and hardware teams to define repeatable processes for new data center builds and lead hands-on operations to uphold the performance and reliability of our deployed infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define and execute sequences of operations, commissioning steps, and bring-up processes for mission-critical data center facilities.

  • Manage monitoring, maintenance, and quality control of the data center infrastructure, including high-performance liquid cooling systems.

  • Develop on-site operations staffing strategy.

  • Develop and enforce procedures for planed and unplanned downtime and SLAs for critical facility components.

Qualifications

More than 90,000 real estate professionals, including over 30% of the WSJ Real Trends top 100 agents in the United States, use us to run and grow their business.

The Opportunity

We're hiring a Senior DevOps Engineer to build the AI-native, self-service infrastructure platform that powers how Luxury Presence ships software. It's a platform where every developer, human or agent, can validate a change in minutes, understand failures immediately, and ship confidently.

You'll join a small, high-leverage Infrastructure team with a clear mandate: multiply what every engineer and agent can do through automation, self-service, and guardrails-by-design. The goal is a platform where self-service is the default and human intervention is the exception, and you'll help make that real.

What You'll Do

  • Build and operate the self-service infrastructure platform. Make the right thing the easy thing, and the secure thing the default.

  • Build the golden paths engineers and agents ship on. Within a technical direction set by the team's Staff engineers, build and operate the layers they rely on (a unified CI/CD pipeline, GitOps-based delivery with ArgoCD, an IaC module catalog, and scaffolding for new services), owning specific components end to end. The goal is for engineers and agents to provision infrastructure and ship changes within guardrails, without hand-writing Terraform/Kustomize or waiting on a ticket.

  • Make agents first-class developers. Help generalize our agent isolation pattern into reusable platform primitives: sandboxed runtime, workload identity, audit trails, and approval gates. Every agent action runs on the same identity, audit, ownership, cost-attribution, and approval rails as a human.

  • Build and operate the validation platform and quality gates. Provide the rails that teams validate changes on before production: ephemeral PR environments with auto-teardown, plus the security, performance, and load-testing gates developers rely on. Implement new gates as coverage grows, keep them fast and low-flake, and drive services onto them. Make gate and test results machine-readable and callable outside the PR flow, so agents and humans alike can act on a failure directly.

  • Own the reliability and observability of what you build. Create the dashboards and operational controls that make the surfaces you own observable and improvable as throughput grows: gate pass rates, approval-rate and self-service-ratio trends, common failure modes, cost attribution, and DORA metrics surfaced to teams. Carry on-call for those surfaces and run incidents from detection through follow-up, turning recurring toil into automation and runbooks other engineers reuse.

What We're Looking For

  • Senior-level experience in SRE, DevOps, or Platform Engineering. You've built and operated production infrastructure at scale and can own a significant workstream end to end with limited oversight.

  • An active, opinionated use of AI development tools (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) in your own infrastructure workflow: Terraform changes, Kubernetes debugging, automation, operational investigations. You have a point of view on where these tools help and where they don't.

  • Deep Kubernetes (EKS) and AWS experience (IAM, VPC, ECR, SSM/Secrets Manager, S3, SQS, Lambda, RDS/Aurora).

  • Strong IaC (Terraform) and GitOps experience, including PR-driven apply workflows (Atlantis or similar) and ArgoCD.

  • CI/CD depth (GitHub Actions), including caching/parallelism, artifact management, test reliability, and pipeline observability.

  • Full incident-ownership experience: you've carried on-call for systems you built and driven incidents from detection through follow-up.

  • Excellent cross-team communication: you can translate platform constraints into developer-friendly solutions and documentation.

Bonus Points

  • Identity, access, and policy-as-code experience: workload/service identity (SPIFFE/SPIRE, OIDC), short-lived credentials, secrets management (Vault), and policy enforcement.

  • Experience building self-service developer platforms, ephemeral environments, CLIs, scaffolding tools, or internal developer portals (Backstage or custom). You treat infrastructure as a product.

  • Cost-awareness: you've built cost attribution, budgets, or rightsizing into a platform.

Our Tech Stack

Infrastructure: AWS, EKS, Terraform (with Atlantis), Vault, Docker, OPA (Open Policy Agent).

CI/CD: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD + Kustomize (GitOps).

Messaging: Kafka (Confluent Cloud).

Observability: Datadog, OpenTelemetry.

Languages/Apps: Node.js/TypeScript microservices, Python, React front-ends.

Compensation

Additional Information

Join us in shaping the future of real estate

The real estate industry is in the midst of a seismic shift, and the future belongs to those who break new ground. As one of the fastest-growing companies in the proptech and marketing sectors, Luxury Presence challenges the status quo of what technology can do for real estate agents, leaders, and brokerages.

More than 18,000 real estate businesses rely on our platform, including 30% of the Wall Street Journal RealTrends top agents and teams. Additionally, many of the industry's most powerful brokerages rely on Luxury Presence as a trusted business partner.

Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

*Note: This position requires presence in our San Francisco, San Jose, or Bellevue office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

The Role

Lambda’s Core Cloud Platform organization builds the software and services that turn large-scale GPU infrastructure into reliable, customer-facing cloud products. The team owns foundational platform capabilities across Managed Kubernetes, resource lifecycle, workload orchestration, cloud APIs, automation, observability, and multi-region operations.

The immediate focus for this role includes evolving Lambda’s Managed Kubernetes platform: making it easier and safer to provision, upgrade, operate, and scale Kubernetes clusters for demanding AI workloads. The platform integrates closely with Lambda’s underlying compute, networking, storage, fleet, and security systems.

As Engineering Manager, you will lead a team building and operating these foundational platform services. You will own the team’s people, execution, technical quality, and production outcomes while partnering with senior engineers to set technical direction. This is a high-leverage role at the intersection of cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, Kubernetes, and the customer experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the design, implementation, and production operation of foundational cloud-platform services.

  • Own the technical roadmap for making the platform more distributed, resilient, observable, and operationally efficient.

  • Ensure the platform operates reliably across a growing multi-datacenter and multi-region fleet, including appropriate handling of partial failures and long-running workflows.

  • Partner with senior and staff engineers to make sound architectural decisions across distributed services, stateful systems, APIs, schedulers, controllers, and automation.

  • Define clear contracts and integration patterns between the cloud platform and the compute, networking, fleet, security, and customer-facing systems around it.

  • Lead and grow a team of senior and staff engineers; hire exceptionally, develop people, maintain a high-performance bar, and address underperformance directly.

  • Own project planning, prioritization, and delivery aligned with Lambda’s business objectives and customer commitments.

  • Establish strong engineering practices across design reviews, testing, CI/CD, observability, incident response, and on-call operations.

  • Collaborate with peer Engineering Managers and cross-functional partners to resolve dependencies and deliver complete customer outcomes.

  • Improve engineering leverage through automation, effective operating mechanisms, and responsible use of AI-assisted engineering.

  • Stay current with developments in Kubernetes, cloud-native infrastructure, GPU orchestration, and platform automation, and apply them where they materially improve Lambda’s platform.

You

  • 4+ years of engineering management experience with a demonstrated track record of growing high-performing teams

  • 7+ years of software engineering IC experience, including principal or staff-level ownership of mission-critical distributed systems

  • 8+ years implementing business-critical services in Python or Go, from conception through production

  • Experience building systems that coordinate across multiple independently-owned infrastructure services (compute, networking, storage) without owning them directly

  • Background in multi-region deployment strategies, cross-datacenter state management, and high-availability architectures

  • Strong track record of owning projects end-to-end: architecture, delivery, operations, and continuous improvement

  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration - proven ability to drive alignment across infrastructure, platform, and product teams

Nice to Have

  • Awareness of the evolving bare metal and GPU infrastructure ecosystem - including tools like NVIDIA NiCo (NCX Infra Controller) for DPU-enforced lifecycle automation, BlueField DPU capabilities, and where industry standards for multi-tenant bare metal management are heading

  • Experience evaluating or adopting vendor infrastructure tooling into an existing platform - performing a full migration, having the judgment to assess fit, risk, and timing

  • Familiarity with Kubernetes or Slurm - useful context for how this team integrates with Lambda’s cluster orchestration layer, but not required for the role itself

  • Experience in the AI, ML, or GPU hardware industry

  • Proven track record designing large-scale cloud IaaS platforms from the ground up

  • Exposure to IPO readiness, enterprise compliance, or security requirements at scale

Values We’re Looking For

  • Hands-on when needed: You can get into the details when the team or system needs it without becoming the long-term bottleneck.

  • High accountability: You take responsibility for delivery and production outcomes and do not tolerate systems remaining unreliable.

  • Business and customer alignment: You connect technical priorities to the outcomes that matter for Lambda and its customers.

  • Sound judgment: You make decisions with incomplete information, manage risk, and change direction when the evidence changes.

  • Systems builder: You create teams, processes, and technical foundations that operate effectively without depending on constant intervention.

  • Agency with context: You find responsible paths through obstacles without creating unnecessary risk or operating as a cowboy.

  • Low ego and strong collaboration: You handle disagreement directly, learn when you are wrong, and build productive cross-functional relationships.

  • Learning through failure: You turn operational and organizational failures into stronger systems and lasting improvements.

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

You will own critical capabilities spanning container image security, Kubernetes platform operations, authentication services, and infrastructure automation; while continuously driving down manual toil through AI-assisted automation.

  • Cloud Infrastructure: Strong AWS cloud foundation, with production experience in ECS, EKS, IAM, and Security Hub services.

At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. How will you make an impact?

  • We are seeking a highly skilled, technically authoritative and customer-facing Sr. Principal Hyperscale Rack Engineer within the Intelligent Infrastructure Segment to lead the architecture, integration, and strategic direction of advanced air and liquid-cooled server and network rack solutions for large-scale hyperscale deployments.

  • This role will serve as the senior technical authority responsible for translating customer requirements into scalable, manufacturable, and commercially viable rack systems.

  • As the Sr. Principal Hyperscale Rack Engineer, youwill operate at the intersection of engineering, customer engagement, and program execution – driving end-to-end rack architecture across mechanical, power, thermal, electrical, and software domains.

  • Success in this role requires deep technical expertise, strong commercial acumen, and the ability to lead complex programs while influencing both internal and external stakeholders.

What will you do?

  • Serve as the lead architect and development manager for complex rack-level solutions, owning system-level design decisions across mechanical, electrical, power, thermal, networking, and software integration domains.

  • Lead customer-facing technical engagements from RFI/RFQ all the way to first hardware delivery, including design reviews, trade-off discussions, and executive-level conversations.

  • Translate ambiguous or evolving customer requirements into clear program frameworks, ensuring alignment between customer expectations and engineering execution.

  • Demonstrate strong commercial awareness by effectively managing customer expectations, pushing back when requirements introduce risk or inefficiency, and confidently addressing challenging technical and cost-related questions.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment across all departments (executives, engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and program) to ensure cohesive solution development with emphasis on Bill of Materials (BOM) management and scheduling.

  • Own rack-level architecture including power distribution design, thermal strategies (air and liquid cooling), cable routing, serviceability, and manufacturability.

  • Provide deep technical guidance on rack infrastructure including PDUs, busbars, liquid cooling systems (CDUs, manifolds, QDs), airflow design, and high-density compute integration.

  • Oversee architecture decisions impacting performance, cost, scalability, and deployment efficiency.

  • Drive program execution from concept through production, ensuring schedules are clearly defined, tracked, and met.

  • Apply strong program management discipline: define milestones, identify risks early, escalate issues proactively, and hold cross-functional teams accountable to commitments.

  • Drive readiness support calls internally from initial NPI scoping to prototyping to mass production, ensuring all systems are operable together from a power, thermal, and software standpoint.

  • Partner with customers and internal stakeholders to continuously refine designs based on deployment feedback and operational learnings.

  • Collaborate with compliance and certification teams to ensure mechanical designs meet global regulatory requirements (e.g., UL, CE, ISTA, ASTM).

  • Mentor and guide engineers across disciplines, establishing best practices in rack system architecture and integration.

  • Understanding of rack installation constraints, maintenance access, and serviceability in rack mechanical infrastructure.

  • Conduct root cause analysis and corrective actions for mechanical failures or field issues.

  • May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

How will you get here?

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related field is required

Experience:

  • Minimum of 10 years’ experience in engineering, systems integration, or data center hardware design.

  • Minimum of 3 years’ rack-level (L11) solution design and integration experience.

  • Proven ability to drive the development and execution of complex rack solutions for hyperscale or large-scale data center environments, managing 12-18 month lifecycles and portfolios valued at hundreds of millions of dollars.

  • Familiarity with industry standards (EIA, ORV3, OCP) and global power architectures.

  • Demonstrated experience working directly with customers in technical and commercially sensitive environments.

  • Strong background in program execution, including schedule ownership, risk management, and cross-functional leadership.

  • Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills – a must.

  • Strong understanding of mechanical systems, integration strategies, and program management.

  • Hands-on experience with prototype fabrication and testing (mechanical S&V, software burn-in and test validation).

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

  • Capable of assessing projects, articulating risks, and developing project milestones.

  • Creative, self-motivated, accountable, and team-oriented.

  • Able to work independently with minimal oversight.

  • Skilled in writing reports, business correspondence, and procedural guides.

  • Effective at presenting information and responding to management, clients, and public queries.

  • Capable of influencing others and sharing best practices.

  • Familiar with stage-gate processes in project lifecycle management (PLM).

  • Able to coach and mentor less experienced engineers.

  • Demonstrated success leading in a highly matrixed environment, driving alignment and execution across cross-functional teams without direct reporting authority.

  • Ability to travel both domestically and internationally up to 30%.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Master’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related field is preferred.

  • Proficiency in CAD tools (e.g., SolidWorks, Creo/Pro-E, Inventor) and FEA software (e.g., ANSYS, Abaqus).

data.title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps Remote, worldwide
data.description:
Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps

Remote, worldwide · Freelance course project with a path to full-time

We’re hiring on behalf of a global hands-on tech-education platform used by over a million engineers to learn DevOps, cloud, Kubernetes and AI. Its courses are built around real labs, not slides, and taught by practising engineers who are great on camera.

We’re looking for a DevOps engineer who loves teaching to create and present a course on AI for DevOps: how engineers use AI agents and modern AI tooling in real infrastructure work.

This role suits you if you already teach as part of what you do: you’ve published courses on Udemy, Pluralsight or YouTube, written a book, worked in DevRel, run workshops, or regularly speak at meetups and conferences.

How it works

  • It starts with one paid course project. You can do it alongside your current job. There’s no fixed weekly-hour requirement, just a delivery plan you agree on together. A typical project takes around 3 months.

  • The goal is long-term. The team is growing its internal trainer pool, and the first project is how both sides find out if it’s a fit. After that, it can lead to a full-time role or more course projects.

  • A fixed fee per course is agreed upfront, based on course length and topic complexity. Fees are competitive, and advanced topics and exceptional instructors are paid accordingly. Payment is made on delivery of the completed course.

  • Fully remote with flexible hours. Expect a weekly sync, Slack communication, and some time-zone overlap with a Europe/Asia-based team.

What you’ll do

  • Shape the course with the curriculum team: sections, lessons, and hands-on labs.

  • Write lab specs that a dedicated labs team builds, then test them.

  • Write and narrate short, story-driven video lessons (about 6 minutes each). You’re welcome to use AI to draft, but the final script should sound like you.

  • Record demo and lab-solution walkthroughs.

  • Work through structured editorial feedback, especially on your first section.

Video editing, animation, lab infrastructure and publishing are all handled by the production team. You focus on the teaching.

What we’re looking for

  • Hands-on DevOps foundations: Linux, containers, Kubernetes, a major cloud, CI/CD, IaC. You build and run infrastructure yourself.

  • Real, current use of AI in your engineering work: AI agents, coding assistants, LLM-based automation. Deep AI specialisation isn’t required, but curiosity and staying current are.

  • Excellent spoken and written English. All courses are scripted, narrated and delivered in English, so you need clear, natural, easily understood English and confidence on camera.

  • A genuine passion for teaching, shown through courses, tutorials, talks, workshops or mentoring you’ve done because you enjoy it.

  • The ability to explain complex topics simply, with empathy for beginners.

  • Clear, engaging spoken English and confidence on camera.

About Eve
Eve is redefining legal technology for plaintiff law firms, and we're building the team that will take us there. We help firms handle more cases, recover more for clients, and grow with AI that works across every stage of a case, from intake through resolution. The next generation of great plaintiff firms will be AI-Native, and Eve is how they get there. But what makes Eve different isn't just the product. It's how we build it. If you're someone who takes ownership, stays curious, and wants to build AI that's already changing how law is practiced, this is where you belong.

Product-market fit: Eve is trusted by over 1000+ law firms, and we’re growing fast.
Backed by top investors: We’ve raised over $160M from world-class partners including Spark Capital, Andreessen Horowitz(A16z), Menlo Ventures, and Lightspeed.
Built by a world-class team: Engineers, designers, and operators from places like Scale, Meta, Airbnb, Cruise, Square, Rubrik, and Lyft are building Eve from the ground up.
AI-Native from day one: We’re on the bleeding edge of AI, collaborating directly with teams at OpenAI and Anthropic to build best-in-class AI workflows tailored for legal work.
Explosive growth: We are growing 2X revenue Quarter over Quarter.

The Role

We're hiring a Staff Analytics Engineer to own Eve's go-to-market data model and set the standard the rest of the analytics engineering team works inside.

The number of people asking the data a question is growing faster than the business, and the business is doubling. Today the same question can produce different answers depending on who asks and which tool they open. Your job is to make every core GTM metric resolve to one governed definition: pipeline generated, funnel conversion, CAC, win rate, sales cycle length, ARR and bookings, modeled in the warehouse and semantic layer from HubSpot, DealHub, Apollo, and Clay rather than inside those tools.

As the Staff engineer, GTM is your domain but not your limit. You'll own the certification framework and catalog that determine what counts as trusted across every domain, set the modeling standards other analytics engineers and analysts build inside, and make the calls when two teams define the same thing differently. Your users span analysts and stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, CS, and RevOps.

You'll work on our central team and report to the Head of Data Engineering, who reports directly to the CEO. Data is a first-class function at Eve and the fuel to drive our future growth.

What You'll Do

Model GTM

  • Partner with analysts and stakeholders to build the models that power Eve's GTM decisions: pipeline, funnel, campaign, and revenue, sourced from HubSpot, DealHub, Apollo, and Clay and built in the warehouse and semantic layer rather than inside those tools
  • Design semantic models for core GTM SaaS metrics (pipeline coverage, funnel conversion, CAC, win rate, sales cycle time, ARR and bookings), then own deploying and maintaining them as the trusted foundation for both analytics and AI consumption
  • Build on the foundational layer the data engineers own: source-to-staging models and conformed dimensions.
  • Instrument your models against the team's alerting so failures and drift surface before a stakeholder finds them
  • Maintain documentation of the models, metrics, and definitions you own
  • Stand up internal AI agents and data-grounded tools that give GTM stakeholders a direct, trustworthy answer without waiting on a ticket

Set the standard

  • Own the metrics certification framework and catalog: what qualifies as a governed definition, who owns it, and how a stakeholder can tell at a glance
  • Define the modeling standards and semantic layer patterns every analytics engineer and contributing analyst works inside
  • Partner with analysts building on the semantic layer, and own the certification call on what becomes a governed definition
  • Arbitrate when two teams define the same metric differently, and make the call stick
  • Establish patterns and standards for analytical application development in Omni and Hex
  • Sit with stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to turn open questions into durable models rather than one-off answers
  • Mentor analytics engineers and set the technical bar for how analytics engineering gets done at Eve

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years in analytics engineering, including time at a staff or senior IC level setting technical direction others followed
  • Extensive proficiency in SQL, data modeling, and transformation, with deep dbt expertise: advanced modeling patterns, macros, packages, and testing. Experience building SCD tables from multiple sources
  • Expert knowledge of the modern stack: Snowflake, dbt, and a semantic or BI layer such as Omni or Hex
  • Experience designing semantic models or metric layers for human and AI consumption
  • Experience modeling GTM systems (HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar CRM and marketing automation platforms)
  • You've resolved a "these numbers don't match" problem across teams that each believed their version, and can describe how you got everyone to one definition
  • Experience setting modeling standards others follow, and reviewing contributions from people outside your team

The Role

Eve is doubling revenue quarter over quarter, and the platform is being built to keep pace. A medallion architecture is in place on a Terraform-managed Snowflake footprint. Most of what goes on top is still ahead: ingestion and orchestration built for the volume coming, reliability practice, the access and governance model, and the standards every contributor works inside.

The data spans product usage, case and firm data, and every go-to-market system Eve runs on. Analytics engineers and business analysts build models and reporting on top of it, AI agents query it directly, and leadership makes calls on it weekly. When a pipeline fails quietly, all three inherit the mistake.

You'll own the pipelines carrying all of that, end to end, from an ambiguous ask through to production. Moving nightly rebuilds onto incremental patterns. Deciding how a new source gets ingested and what happens when it changes shape. Building the alerting that catches a broken model before anyone downstream does, and being the one who picks it up when it breaks.

You'll have real say in how the platform gets built. You'll work on our central team and report to the Head of Data Engineering, who reports directly to the CEO. Data is a first-class function at Eve and the fuel to drive our future growth.

What You'll Do

Build and run the platform

  • Own ingestion through Fivetran, third-party connectors, and custom extraction where no connector exists
  • Own orchestration across dbt platform and GitHub Actions, own materialization strategy and model performance, move critical models off nightly full rebuilds onto incremental patterns, and cut latency where decisions are waiting on stale data
  • Build source-schema change detection, so an upstream field change surfaces as an alert before it reaches a report
  • Stand up observability: freshness SLAs on critical tables, alerting on failure and drift, and an incident path with clear ownership
  • Be a first responder when pipelines break, and drive the fix upstream so the same failure doesn't recur
  • Manage pipeline compute cost, and make the tradeoffs between freshness and spend explicit rather than accidental
  • Share Snowflake administration: implementing the role-based access model, security and network policies, data masking and PII controls, and storage organization
  • Extend the medallion architecture and the Terraform-managed footprint, including full separation of development and production
  • Contribute to the foundational modeling layer the Analytics Engineers build on: source-to-staging patterns, conformed dimensions, shared entities, and SCD patterns that make history reliable

Raise the bar

  • Build and maintain the development environments and CI that let analysts contribute models safely, and review their contributions so more of the company can build on the foundation
  • Build the tooling and setup that gets a new engineer or analyst productive in days, not weeks
  • Administer the data tooling stack: access, integrations, and the connective work between systems
  • Use AI-assisted development as part of how you work: Claude Code skills, agents, and evals, held to the same review bar as anything else

  • Practical dbt: incremental models, testing, macros, and a git-based workflow with CI. Experience building SCD tables from multiple sources

  • You've built reliability practice where none existed: alerting, freshness SLAs, incident response, schema change detection

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.

The Opportunity 

As a Sr. Data Engineer at Oportun, you will be a key member of our team, responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining sophisticated software / data platforms in achieving the charter of the engineering group. Your mastery of a technical domain enables you to take up business problems and solve them with a technical solution. With your depth of expertise and leadership abilities, you will actively contribute to architectural decisions, mentor junior engineers, and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality, scalable software solutions that advance our impact in the market. This is a role where you will have the opportunity to take up responsibility in leading the technology effort – from technical requirements gathering to final successful delivery of the product - for large initiatives (cross-functional and multi-month-long projects).

At Oportun, we move fast and we hold each other to a high bar. If you care about doing your best work while actually moving the needle for real people, you'll fit right in.

What You'll Do

Your day-to-day

  • You’ll design and implement scalable, efficient, and reliable data architectures that support business and analytical needs.
  • You’ll build and maintain data pipelines, ETL processes, and integration solutions for large volumes of structured and unstructured data.
  • You’ll optimize data pipelines, databases, data warehouses, and data lakes for performance, reliability, scalability, and security.
  • You’ll partner with stakeholders to understand data requirements, develop domain expertise, and translate business needs into effective data models and solutions.
  • You’ll establish and improve data quality standards, validation rules, documentation, and governance practices.
  • You’ll implement monitoring and observability practices to identify bottlenecks, improve performance, and strengthen platform reliability.
  • You’ll provide technical leadership on architecture, scalability, reliability, monitoring, integration, and extensibility.
  • You’ll lead and contribute to code reviews, helping maintain high standards for code quality, performance, and maintainability.
  • You’ll mentor junior engineers and support a culture of continuous learning and technical excellence.
  • You’ll take ownership of production issues, including troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, escalation, and long-term resolution.
  • You’ll independently lead multiple features and projects, coordinate work across engineers, and keep stakeholders informed of progress, risks, and dependencies.
  • You’ll help evolve engineering tools, platforms, and practices and encourage adoption of better ways of working.
  • You’ll look for practical ways to use AI tools to improve engineering productivity, analysis, documentation, and problem-solving.

Who You Are

The right fit looks like this

You’re a hands-on data engineer who enjoys solving complex technical problems and building systems that others depend on. You combine strong technical depth with a practical understanding of business needs and know how to turn ambiguous requirements into scalable solutions.

You take ownership, communicate clearly, and are comfortable leading technical work without relying on formal authority. You enjoy mentoring others and helping teams make stronger technical decisions.

What You Bring

Skills & experience

Required

  • 8+ years of experience in data engineering, with strong experience in data architecture, ETL, and database management.
  • Strong programming skills in Python or PySpark, plus experience with Java or Scala.
  • Experience building complex end-to-end data pipelines and data integration solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of SQL and experience with relational and NoSQL database technologies.
  • Experience with big data technologies such as Spark, Kafka, Hadoop, or similar platforms.
  • Experience with orchestration and scheduling tools such as Airflow, Databricks, Jenkins, or similar technologies.
  • Experience designing and operating scalable, reliable, and secure data systems.
  • Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP and associated data services.
  • Experience working in Agile environments such as Scrum, Lean, or Kanban.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • Experience mentoring junior engineers and contributing to technical leadership within a team.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

Nice to Have

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field.
  • Databricks experience or certification.
  • Experience with AWS Redshift, S3, Azure SQL Data Warehouse, or comparable cloud data services.
  • Experience implementing data governance, data quality, or observability frameworks.
  • Experience leading cross-functional or multi-month engineering initiatives.
  • Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools to improve development, troubleshooting, documentation, or productivity.

Our AI Mindset

We build with AI. We lead with judgment.

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work.

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting, willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle.

In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together.

data.description:
Greater Good Charities is a 501(c)(3) global nonprofit organization that works to help people, pets, and the planet by mobilizing in response to need and amplifying the good. To date, we have provided over $1B in aid, expertise, and funding in 121 countries in support of this mission.

Position Overview:

The Director of Supply Chain is a high-impact, hands-on operational leader and strategic troubleshooter. Operating at the intersection of supply chain execution, data analytics, and program strategy, this role is built to drive rapid operational optimization across GGC's global distribution engine.

You will lead the end-to-end movement of donated (in-kind) and procured goods, balancing immediate operational pragmatism with long-term systems modernization. Embedded within a data-driven programmatic architecture that prioritizes evidence for decision-making, you will design agile inventory frameworks, establish demand forecasting, and enforce supply chain best practices tailored for non-governmental organizations.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Agile Inventory Management & Demand Planning

  • Design, implement, and maintain responsive demand planning models that seamlessly bridge internal program planning and donor pipelines with global suppliers, downstream partner capacities, and community needs.
  • Establish agile inventory control protocols to ensure real-time visibility, optimize stock rotation, minimize warehousing overhead, and mitigate product expiration risks.
  • Structure and manage a pre-positioned Disaster Response Reserve, ensuring rapid deployment capability during acute emergency responses without disrupting ongoing core distribution.

2. End-to-End Supply Chain Execution (70% US / 30% International)

  • Direct the full operational lifecycle of goods: donor offer matching, multi-modal freight contracting (TL, LTL, Ocean, Air), field receiving, inventory verification, distribution, and financial closeout.
  • US Domestic Logistics (70%): Oversee recipient partner networks and warehouse operations, establishing industry best practices for safety, pest control, receiving, capacity planning, and field training.
  • European & International Operations (30%): Direct cross-border logistics, import/export requirements, and customs compliance for international shipments, ensuring specialized frameworks like the EU Goods program meet regional standards.
  • European Capacity Expansion Strategy: Develop and execute a strategic capacity growth plan to absorb, manage, and scale corporate and in-kind donations across Europe through a robust, sustainable supply chain framework.
  • Own carrier and broker relationships, negotiating competitive rates, monitoring SLAs, and managing detention, damage, and freight claims.

3. Systems Integration, Data Architecture & Decision Intelligence

  • Serve as the operational business owner for GGC’s logistics tech stack (Salesforce, NetSuite ERP, Smartsheet, SharePoint, and WMS), maximizing system efficiency and tool interconnectivity to deliver streamlined procedures, reduced cycle times, and accurate financial reporting.
  • Eliminate manual data re-keying by standardizing data intake forms, partner reporting portals, and digital field submissions, leveraging lightweight, right-sized AI-powered solutions to automate document processing and field data capture.
  • Transform raw supply chain and field data into actionable intelligence, building real-time executive dashboards tracking key operational metrics (e.g., report timeliness, cycle times, accept/decline rates, pledged vs. received accuracy, and net landed impact).

4. Process Troubleshooting & Pragmatic SOP Optimization

  • Act as a pragmatic troubleshooter across the supply chain, identifying bottlenecks, resolving operational friction, and bridging gaps between field realities and formal policy.
  • Develop, consolidate, and enforce unified Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for movement tracking, inventory control, and bill of lading (BOL) submission pathways.
  • Balance practical field solutions with necessary system upgrades, ensuring new workflows remain user-friendly for field partners while adhering to strict institutional controls.

5. Financial Reconciliation & Compliance Governance

  • Partner with Finance to ensure 100% alignment between physical inventory movement, field receipt documentation, and the general ledger.
  • Streamline the financial closeout and reconciliation cycle time for in-kind shipments and handling fee invoices.
  • Maintain IRS-ready documentation (Form 990 / Form 8282 standards), enforce strict no-resale policies, manage recall protocols, and support internal and external financial/programmatic audits.
  • Ensure compliance with U.S. export control and sanctions regulations (EAR/OFAC) for international shipments, including denied-party screening of partners, vendors, and recipients.

6. Partner Capacity Building

  • Establish performance criteria, quality scorecards, and audit frameworks for domestic and international distribution partners, implementing systematic approaches to collect, analyze, and act upon audit findings.
  • Create user-friendly onboarding toolkits, digital training modules, and technical support pathways for field teams, program focal points, and community distribution networks.
  • Recommend corrective action protocols (probation, suspension, or offboarding) when partner compliance or safety standards are compromised.

7. Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Build, mentor, and direct the global logistics team, establishing a clear staffing model and career progression pathways.
  • Serve as a collaborative team player and primary operational liaison between Logistics, Programs, Finance, Operations, and Corporate Relations, translating complex supply chain data into strategic recommendations for C-Suite leadership.

Minimum Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field required (Master’s degree a plus).
  • 10+ years of progressive leadership in global supply chain and logistics management.
  • Professional certification such as APICS/ASCM CSCP or CPIM, ISM CPSM, or Certified Humanitarian Logistician (CHL) strongly preferred.
  • Proven track record as a hands-on "troubleshooter" capable of making swift, practical decisions in fast-paced NGO or humanitarian environments.
  • Strong team-building skills with a highly collaborative approach to cross-departmental work.
  • Demonstrated experience with ERPs (NetSuite), CRMs (Salesforce), and WMS platforms.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Proven ability to bridge everyday operational tools (e.g., spreadsheets, Smartsheet) by embedding them into enterprise systems and AI-assisted workflows to boost efficiency and user adoption.
  • Expertise in US freight and warehousing networks (70%), combined with practical knowledge of international cross-border logistics, customs, and international trade compliance (30%).
  • Solid understanding of inventory valuation, audit readiness, financial reconciliation, and managing donor-restricted goods.
  • High initiative and strategic thinking, with the ability to balance immediate operational field demands with long-term organizational transformation.
  • Commitment to the mission of Greater Good Charities.

Working Environment:

This position is fully remote. The employee is expected to work 40 hours per week from 9 am – 5 pm in their time zone, Monday – Friday. Travel: 30% (includes domestic & international)

Benefits:

Benefits include 13 paid national holidays, sick leave, paid vacation, parental leave, 401K, life insurance, medical, dental, and vision benefits.

Salary: $94,000-126,000

data.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

YOUR ROLE

You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.

Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.

We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

  • Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier
  • Carrier conversion data running in production models
  • Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale
  • A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions
  • Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives
  • Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

  • 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact
  • Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.
  • You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included
  • You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift
  • You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view
  • Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

  • Real ad budget spent in live auctions
  • Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems
  • Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms
  • Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration
  • Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior
  • AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker
  • CI/CD deployment

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

Since day one, we've been committed to having a diverse, inclusive team and culture. We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity company. We value diversity, equity, and inclusion.

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Apply directly on RemoteJobs.org: https://remotejobs.org/remote-jobs/staff-data-scientist-lead-generation-launch-potato
